title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation  [ the process of becoming like Jesus] part 16
scripture_text: ‘’Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word should share all good things with their instructor. Do not be deceived God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows. Whoever sows to please their flesh from the flesh will reap destruction; whoever sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life. Let us not become weary in doing good for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.’’
devotional:
Let us look at this passage and try and discover the kind of seeds we should be sowing

Seeds of learning. We need to be people that long to learn.

The first relationship that Paul talks about is the relationship between those who teach the word of God and those who are taught. Galatians 6:6. As Christians we should always have a teachable attitude. If someone at school engages well with a teacher, they are probably going to enjoy the class more and perhaps learn more. This same principle applies to the church. The question is, are we teachable? What does it mean to be teachable? To help us grasp what Paul is saying there are two words that he uses that may help us.

[a] The first word for teach katēcheō, which was used in the sense of reporting something to another or to instruct someone, it was used to described an actor speaking down from a stage, and it is where our word echo is derived from. Paul uses it four times and uses it exclusively to refer to instructing someone in the Christian faith (1 Cor 14:19; Gal 6:6 [2x]; Rom 2:18). It is from this word that we get our word catechism. a summary of the principles of Christian religion in the form of questions and answers, used for religious instruction. So we need to be people who have continual eagerness to learn truth that will define our lives.

Can I just say that being teachable is a choice, it is an intentional attitude, a deliberate mindset.

Let us take a step back and think about this. How do we listen to teaching from the word of God, what frame of mind do we have as we sit listening to sermons every week? We can either sit and be or not be engaged, thinking about lots of other things, or, we can sit with a teachable heart, longing to learn about God and ourselves.

[b] The second word Paul uses is koinoneo which means to share, not to impart but share, to have things in common, to hold in common, the word was used as business partners. Paul is saying that learning is a corporate experience, where we choose to invest in order to learn. The focus of this verse is the quality of the relationship between the teacher and those he is teaching. We need to be personally and proactively be investing some of our resources so we can have more opportunity to learn about God and know him better.

For the Christian learning to know God for the most part will be a painful and difficult experience, because it will require all our false and wrong understandings about God [which often feel like truth,] to be demolished. It may require a deconstruction of some of our theology in order to build a more biblical theology that is more consistent with who God really is.

How do you know if you are teachable?

You have a curiosity to learn, you’ll be conscious that you have so much more to learn.

You listen to others carefully and patiently with a desire to learn from everyone.

You read widely especially outside your theological comfort zone.

You’re prepared to move out of your comfort zone, try something different, make mistakes, look stupid, answer wrongly, etc.

You don’t give up when you fail at something, but seek help, and try again and again until you get it right.

You are willing to change your views and practices when convincing evidence is presented to you, even if it means admitting you were wrong.
prayer: Father thank you that life is being enrolled in a life long classroom.
